title: Pick a Color
body:
Goal: the program asks for a color and paints a circle in that color. If it does not know the color, it says so and uses black.

  1. Open starter.py and press Run (F5). Type orange in the Shell and press Return. It works!
  2. Run again and type green. A red error! The program does not know green yet.
  3. Add an elif for "green" (use "#009E73").
  4. Add an else: for any other answer: print a friendly message and use black "#000000".
  5. Test all four: orange, blue, green, and something silly like pizza.

Remember: Python is picky - "Blue" and "blue" are different. Type small letters. Each if, elif and else line ends with a colon :, and the lines under it are pushed in 4 spaces.

Done looks like: every answer draws a circle, and the color name is written under it (so you can tell colors apart without seeing color).

Extra: add sky blue ("#56B4E9"), vermillion ("#D55E00") and purple ("#CC79A7").

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Look at the if and elif lines in starter.py. Orange and blue each have their own block, but green does not. That is why green gives a red error.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Add another elif just like the blue one, but for green. Then add an else: at the end. The else: runs when none of the colors above matched, so it catches silly answers like pizza.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: An extra choice looks like elif color_name == "____":, with the color's code on the next line. The catch-all is else:. Under it, print a friendly message and set color to black. Check the colon and the 4 spaces!

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Pick a Color
# The program asks a question, then CHOOSES what to do with if / elif / else.

import turtle

t = turtle.Turtle()
t.shape("turtle")
t.pensize(3)

color_name = input("Pick a color: orange, blue or green? ")

if color_name == "orange":
    color = "#E69F00"
elif color_name == "blue":
    color = "#0072B2"
# TODO: add an elif for "green" (use "#009E73")
# TODO: add an else: print a friendly message and use black "#000000"

# Paint a circle in the chosen color
t.color(color)
t.begin_fill()
t.circle(80)
t.end_fill()

# Write the color name under the circle, so color is not the only clue
t.penup()
t.goto(0, -40)
t.write(color_name, align="center", font=("Arial", 20, "bold"))

turtle.done()
